answer: Positive decisive controls can support the particular one-stage static graph-context target-field allocation recipe. They do not establish a new graph contrastive, feature-alignment, supervised-kernel or sharing principle; useful accuracy can remain an engineering extension.
exact_boundary: All target-distribution dependence reduces to the first fixed-key moment; higher-order Q structure cannot independently affect this loss. Full dictionary geometry still enters the log partition.
closest_new_graph_collision: G-CRD arxiv:2111.04964v4 §§2.2 and 3: node-level teacher/student InfoNCE, learned cosine projection, optional graph-aware auxiliary projection, supervised/logit-KD objective.
candidate_difference: Permanently fixed filtered input keys with no learned GNN teacher, class-conditioned target moments, persistent four-route objective allocation and one common bare auxiliary map. No exact prior match claimed.
graph_specificity_limit: Graph dependence enters key/target construction and the existing SAGE predictor. Existing incidence/uniform controls do not isolate a uniquely topological causal effect or new graph expressivity.
